subject: SIG questionnaire — data retention, logs & training on customer data
body:
From: Susan Mallory <susan.mallory@acme-corp.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: Fri, 22 Aug 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG spreadsheet — questions on data retention & training

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this — attached is our SIG spreadsheet (focused tabs). Two items our procurement/security team would like clarified before we move to legal:
- Do you retain raw prompts or system messages? If so, for how long and in what form?
- Does Redwood ever use customer-provided content (prompts, files, or outputs) to train or improve models? If yes, please describe opt-in/opt-out and any sampling/aggregation controls.

Also, can you point to any evidence (SOC 2, policies, or a short paragraph we can drop into our contract) that we can share with our procurement team?

Thanks — attaching the SIG spreadsheet.

Susan Mallory
Senior Security Analyst
Acme Corp

Subject: Re: SIG spreadsheet — questions on data retention & training

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear list. I've attached a concise response (redwood_sig_response_v1.pdf) and copied our infra/security engineer Neha and lead infra engineer Dev for the technical details below. High level answers up-front:

- Prompt/log retention: By default Redwood retains request and response logs for 30 days to support debugging, abuse detection, and billing reconciliation. Aggregated operational logs (metrics, traces) are retained for 365 days.
- Training: Redwood does NOT use customer content (prompts, files, or outputs) to train or fine-tune models by default. Any use of customer data for model training requires an explicit, documented opt-in (contractual + security review) and is processed under strict controls (sampling, anonymization, limited scope).
- Private/Dedicated: For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers can configure retention and can opt to use customer-managed keys (CMK) — in Private deployments, logs never leave the customer VPC unless explicitly configured.

Evidence: our SOC 2 report and the SIG response PDF are attached; we can also provide a short attestation letter for procurement if useful.

Neha/Dev — can you confirm the encrypted-at-rest details, where prompt logs are stored by default, and the steps to delete account-level logs on request?

Hi Susan / Marissa — quick technical follow-up for the SIG cells that ask for concrete controls. Quoting Marissa's summary below for context: 

> - Prompt/log retention: By default Redwood retains request and response logs for 30 days to support debugging, abuse detection, and billing reconciliation. Aggregated operational logs (metrics, traces) are retained for 365 days.
> - Training: Redwood does NOT use customer content (prompts, files, or outputs) to train or fine-tune models by default. Any use of customer data for model training requires an explicit, documented opt-in (contractual + security review) and is processed under strict controls (sampling, anonymization, limited scope).

Technical clarifications to insert in the SIG: 
1) Storage and encryption: Prompt and response logs are written to an encrypted object store (AES-256) in the region of the request. Keys are either Redwood-managed or customer-managed (KMS/HSM) for Dedicated/Private. All access to logs is audited via immutable audit logs (IAM + SIEM forwarding).
2) Retention windows: Default application request/response logs = 30 days. Debug snapshots (when enabled by customers for support) = configurable up to 90 days. Aggregated telemetry (metrics/traces/alert history) = 365 days. All retention windows are configurable for Dedicated and Private deployments via the Console or API.
3) Training policy: Model training or fine-tuning using customer-provided prompts/attachments is prohibited unless a documented opt-in exists. The opt-in requires: signed contract amendment, security review, and technical controls that include de-identification, limited sampling rate, and explicit dataset provenance. We do not sample nor include customer content in our public or internal model training pipelines without that opt-in.
4) Deletion and subject requests: We support account-level deletion of request logs on request. Delete requests should include Account ID and a timestamp range; the deletion is audited and a deletion confirmation is generated (DR ticket id). For Private deployments, deletion steps are performed by the customer's ops team unless Redwood is engaged under a support contract.

If you want a single-sentence procurement-friendly statement, use: 
"Redwood Inference retains customer request/response logs for 30 days by default and does not use customer-provided content to train models unless there is an explicit, contractual opt-in; retention and key management options are configurable for Dedicated and Private deployments."

Happy to provide a short architecture diagram or the specific SIG cell text for any row.
